title: Procedural activity types — wordsearch, crossword, matching, cloze
summary: Four pure deterministic activity-type generators that don't depend on the LLM. Wordsearch (configurable grid + diagonals on/off + seeded shuffle), crossword (greedy interlocking from clue list), matching (left-right shuffle), cloze (__BLANK__-token-driven extraction). Each emits a `procedural` payload on the section; the renderer + answer-key + print pipeline pick it up.
motivation: Twinkl's praised resource breadth is partly volume but partly format breadth — wordsearch, crossword, matching and cloze are the top-downloaded primary formats. The send-assistant generator emits stems + answer-lines today; these four activity types are entirely missing. They are also the cheapest to ship because they are pure deterministic logic, not LLM calls.

in: shared/aiSchemas.ts — WorksheetSectionSchema additive: type values 'wordsearch'|'crossword'|'matching'|'cloze' + procedural?: { kind, payload }
client/src/components/WorksheetRenderer.tsx — four new render branches (~250 LoC across them)
client/src/lib/promptSections/proceduralActivityDirectives.ts (new, ~80 LoC) — instructs the LLM how to emit a section with the right `procedural` payload when a template (G3) requests one
Targeted vitest per generator (~10 cases each) covering deterministic seed, edge cases (single-word, all-vowel words, very long words)
out: Picture-matching (image-on-left / word-on-right) — deferred; needs an image library which is out of scope
Drag-and-drop interactive variants — deferred to Phase H (depends on G1's interactive surface)
Anagram / sequence-puzzle / mix-and-match — deferred; team can pick later

wordsearch.input: { words: string[]; gridSize?: number; allowDiagonals?: boolean; seed?: number }
wordsearch.output: { grid: string[][]; placements: { word, row, col, dir }[] }
wordsearch.constraint: every word fits; grid is N×N where N = max(maxWordLength + 2, ceil(sqrt(totalLetters * 1.4)))

crossword.constraint: greedy interlocking; rejects any word that cannot interlock; emits a warning per skipped word

matching.output: { left: string[]; right: string[]; key: number[] }
matching.constraint: right column shuffled by seeded LCG; key[i] = original index of right[i]

cloze.input: { prose: string with __BLANK__ tokens; seed?: number }
cloze.output: { rendered: string with [1] [2] tokens; blanks: { num, answer }[]; wordBank?: string[] (shuffled) }

acceptance_criteria: Each generator is pure: same inputs (incl. seed) → identical output across two runs.
Wordsearch grid contains every input word at the recorded placement; no word crosses a grid boundary.
Crossword interlocks ≥70% of input words for randomly-generated 8-word vocab tests; emits one warning per skipped word.
Matching key[] is a valid permutation of [0..n-1]; right column is not in the same order as left.
Cloze blanks count equals the __BLANK__ token count; rendered preserves all non-blank text exactly.
Renderer prints in B&W with intact lines (no SVG-only rendering — table / grid markup so weak printers cope).
Answer-key page (G12) lists every blank's answer + every wordsearch placement + every crossword clue's answer.

risk_register.risk: Crossword greedy algorithm leaves obviously-bad layouts on small word lists
risk_register.mitigation: Algorithm tries 50 seeded restarts and picks the layout that interlocked the most words. Test fixtures lock the expected output for 5 standard vocab lists.

risk_register.risk: Wordsearch with diagonals disabled and many long words doesn't fit
risk_register.mitigation: Generator increases gridSize and retries up to 3 times; emits a warning if it still fails and the section falls back to 'allowDiagonals: true'.

related: G3 — lesson archetypes (Mini-Quiz / Exit-Ticket archetypes can include cloze)
